websites.title: Linear
websites.curatorNote: A benchmark for software websites: restrained, fast, and obsessively sequenced.
websites.breakdown: Study how the page sells a complex product with controlled motion, precise contrast, and product UI that never feels decorative.

websites.title: Stripe
websites.curatorNote: Dense product storytelling without losing elegance or scan speed.
websites.breakdown: Useful for studying section rhythm, technical credibility, and how motion can clarify instead of distract.

websites.title: Arc
websites.curatorNote: A personality-rich software site that still protects the core product story.
websites.breakdown: Notice the balance between playful language, product framing, and immersive page transitions.

websites.title: Raycast
websites.curatorNote: Sharp product density with a strong command-line aesthetic.
websites.breakdown: A strong reference for showing workflows, integrations, and technical sophistication in a compact system.

websites.title: Panic
websites.curatorNote: A studio site with character, clarity, and unmistakable taste.
websites.breakdown: Worth studying for expressive product cards, restrained copy, and personality that never becomes noise.

websites.title: Apple Vision Pro
websites.curatorNote: High-budget product storytelling with immaculate sequencing.
websites.breakdown: Use this to study product reveal timing, cinematic scroll pacing, and premium restraint.

websites.title: Nothing
websites.curatorNote: A commerce experience with a distinct visual rulebook.
websites.breakdown: Strong for studying how brand codes can make ordinary product grids feel collectible.

websites.title: GitHub Copilot
websites.curatorNote: A clear AI product story with developer-native proof points.
websites.breakdown: Useful when designing AI tools that need trust, examples, and practical outcomes over vague magic.

websites.title: Superlist
websites.curatorNote: Bright without feeling cheap; friendly without feeling soft.
websites.breakdown: A good reference for making productivity software feel approachable while keeping visual hierarchy tight.

websites.title: Ordinary Folk
websites.curatorNote: Motion design taste translated into a web portfolio with discipline.
websites.breakdown: Study the timing, whitespace, and how project previews carry the brand more than decoration.

websites.title: Resend
websites.curatorNote: Developer marketing stripped to the essentials without becoming bland.
websites.breakdown: Strong for pricing clarity, code-led product explanation, and sparse interface rhythm.

websites.title: Airbnb Design
websites.curatorNote: Editorial structure for a design org with a high signal-to-noise ratio.
websites.breakdown: A useful model for content-heavy design sites that still need taste and authority.

websites.title: Instrument
websites.curatorNote: A confident agency system that lets work and pacing do the talking.
websites.breakdown: Good for studying editorial hierarchy, large-scale typography, and cinematic case study flow.

websites.title: Gumroad
websites.curatorNote: A rare commerce platform with a visual voice people remember.
websites.breakdown: Worth studying for brand courage, sharp contrast, and how rough edges can become a product asset.

websites.title: Height
websites.curatorNote: Clean AI-assisted workflow storytelling with product UI at the center.
websites.breakdown: A good reference for presenting automation features without losing the core job-to-be-done.

websites.title: Contra
websites.curatorNote: A creator platform with polished cards and a confident marketplace rhythm.
websites.breakdown: Study the way profiles, proof, and calls to action stay legible across a busy marketplace surface.

websites.title: Mubasic
websites.curatorNote: Playful web craft that feels memorable without losing usability.
websites.breakdown: Great for studying cheerful interaction design, rounded pacing, and visual storytelling for non-technical products.

websites.title: Pitch
websites.curatorNote: A crisp SaaS site with a strong grasp of product scenes and page tempo.
websites.breakdown: Useful for studying how to keep a feature-rich product visual and concise across many sections.

websites.title: Readymag
websites.curatorNote: An editorial design tool site that actually behaves like an editorial canvas.
websites.breakdown: Study it for layout courage, typographic contrast, and controlled weirdness.

weeklyDrops.title: Software With Taste
weeklyDrops.description: SaaS sites where product UI, motion, and copy feel designed as one system.

weeklyDrops.title: Motion That Earns Its Place
weeklyDrops.description: Animated references where movement clarifies the idea instead of acting as noise.

weeklyDrops.title: Commerce With a Point of View
weeklyDrops.description: Commerce and product sites that feel distinctive before you read a single line.
